Definition: from G846 and the base of G2237; self-pleasing, i.e. arrogant:--self-willed.
BiblicalUsage: The self-willed are those who please themselves and despise government, and Peter says they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities. Paul says a bishop must not be self-willed, because the overseer is a steward of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that self-will is the root of every other sin on these lists, because it puts my pleasure above God's order.
